short: Britain fought to keep selling opium in China, and won the first of the unequal treaties.
full:
British merchants had balanced their purchases of Chinese tea by shipping Indian opium into Canton in defiance of a Qing ban. In 1839 the imperial commissioner Lin Zexu confined the foreign traders in their factories until they surrendered their stock, and destroyed some twenty thousand chests of it at Humen. Fighting began with a skirmish off Kowloon on 4 September 1839 and escalated when an expeditionary force arrived the following summer.

The war was decided by technology and mobility. The iron steamer Nemesis, drawing little water and independent of the wind, worked up rivers where junks and shore batteries could not answer her, and British troops took Dinghai, the Canton forts, Ningbo and finally Zhenjiang, cutting the Grand Canal. The Treaty of Nanking of 29 August 1842 imposed an indemnity of twenty-one million silver dollars, ceded Hong Kong island, and opened five ports to British residence and trade. A supplementary treaty added extraterritoriality and most-favoured-nation status, terms other powers promptly demanded for themselves.
